iso.provenance: Operator-supplied Windows 11 25H2 x64 English media (not fetched or redistributed by automation). No public download URL is pinned; the builder only verifies the SHA-256 of a pre-staged local file.

installer.provenance: Operator-supplied, downloaded from the operator's NI account (ni.com); not fetched or redistributed by automation.
installer.note: Version 26.5.0 is the overall ISO bundle version, not the LabVIEW application version: the actual LabVIEW package (ni-labview-2026-core-en) is version 26.3.0 / DisplayVersion '2026 Q3', matching the 26.3.x pins used elsewhere in this repo (e.g. vm/ubuntu-labview/provisioning-manifest.json's labview.packageVersion 26.3.1.49165-0+f13). Confirmed 2026-11-02 via `nipkg info ni-labview-2026-core-en` against the mounted ISO's offline feed.

package.note: The ISO is a Debian-style nipkg repository (feeds/<product>/Packages + pool/*.nipkg), not a setup.exe wizard. 'Professional' edition is a licensing distinction applied after this same install (via ni-labview-2026-license), not a different top-level package; there is no separate '-pro' meta-package. Install with: nipkg feed-add --system --name=<name> <driveletter>:\feeds\ni-labview-2026 && nipkg update <name> && nipkg install --accept-eulas --yes --include-recommended ni-labview-2026-core-en.

vipm.verification: This installer build is pinned by SHA-256 as a point-in-time value verified locally on 2026-11-01; JKI publishes new installer builds periodically so the authoritative gate is the Authenticode signer identity, not this hash. Verify with Get-AuthenticodeSignature reporting Status=Valid and SimpleName='James Kring, Inc.', matching docker/windows-sbom/VipmInstallerSignature.ps1.

actionsRunner.verification: SHA-256 independently computed locally on 2026-11-02 from the downloaded asset (not scraped from the release page's rendered checksum list); GitHub publishes a new runner version periodically, so re-pin both fields together when bumping. Used by provision-windows-guest.py's register-runner subcommand to download and verify the runner package inside the guest before Register-WindowsRunner.ps1 configures it.

powershell7.verification: SHA-256 independently computed locally on 2026-11-02 from the downloaded asset. Register-Runner.ps1 (#requires -Version 7.0) needs the real machine-wide MSI, NOT winget's Microsoft.PowerShell package -- that resolves to a broken per-user MSIX stub invisible to the dedicated runner service account (confirmed live during the q3-pro functional proof). provision-windows-guest.py's register-runner subcommand installs this MSI if pwsh isn't already present.

nssm.verification: nssm.cc's own download page explicitly recommends this pre-release build (not the nominal "latest release" 2.24 from 2014-08-31) for "Windows 10 Creators Update or newer" -- which Windows 11 25H2 falls under -- to avoid a documented services-failing-to-start issue in the older build. SHA-256 for both the zip and the extracted win64/nssm.exe independently computed locally on 2026-11-05 from the asset downloaded directly from nssm.cc (the official/canonical source, not a third-party mirror or fork). Used by build-winrm-service-bootstrap-installer.nsi (research prototype for issue #191's own recommended next step: test whether a genuine SCM service, registered the same way the already-proven-safe wuauserv/UsoSvc StartupType disable is, survives the #188 restart where RunOnce/FirstLogonCommands did not).
